records.name: Judīte
records.facts_used: Judīte: The name belongs to the Judith/Judīte family from Hebrew Yehudit, Jewish woman or woman from Judea. Historically it is related to Judah. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.

records.name: Guna
records.facts_used: Guna: Siliņš links Latvian Guna to guns, uguns, flame or fire. A separate documented rendering also gives Swedish Gun as Guna; it does not prove one borrowing route for every Latvian bearer. The local fire-word line is explicitly supported by the Latvian dictionary. Guna is the central character of Aspazija’s play Sidraba šķidrauts. The National Encyclopaedia dates the premiere at the New Latvian Theatre to 27 January 1905, with Otīlija Muceniece as Guna. This is an exact literary-use example, not proof of every later girl’s naming motive.

records.name: Eidimtas
records.facts_used: Eidimtas: The Lithuanian compound contains eid- and imt-. Salys links the first stem group to eiti, to go, and imt- to imti, to take; the modern guide explains eid- through the walking-related eidlus. These are lexical stem connections rather than an invented full sentence. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Eidimtas (Eidas) on 10 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.

records.name: Angelina
records.facts_used: Angelina: Lithuanian Angelina belongs to the Angela family. Its Greek base angelos means messenger and is also used for an angel in Christian tradition. The derived name retains that connection without asserting a person’s character or supernatural qualities. International use of this spelling is illustrated by Angelina Jolie in the Academy’s 2000 award record for her supporting role in Girl, Interrupted. This is a dated foreign namesake example, not the first Lithuanian registration or an explanation of every family’s choice.
